messages:
zach: Hey y'all — new contributor hit a flaky 401 during Ruby quickstart when using bundler/binstub. Happens only when token file is rotated by another process. Minimal repro attached; anyone have experience with forked binstub + auth header caching?

zach: repro gist: ```bash
# start binstub (reads /tmp/rw_token)
RB_TOKEN_FILE=/tmp/rw_token bin/quickstart &
# from another shell after a couple seconds
echo NEW_TOKEN > /tmp/rw_token
```

amy: Which HTTP adapter is sampleapp using? Faraday? httpx? That matters because connection pooling semantics differ.

zach: sampleapp default is Faraday w/ Net::HTTP adapter for CI matrix. Local dev sometimes uses httpx per dev docs. Flake seen on both.

leo: Two likely causes: 1) client instance created before file update holds onto old token in memory, 2) pooled connection keeps an Authorization header at socket level and the first post-rotation request reuses it.

amy: Agreed. Quick mitigation in sampleapp: read token lazily per-request for demo (cheap and clear for newcomers). For prod docs show a pattern to invalidate the pool.

zach: Sketch of conservative fix in SDK: add TokenStrategy module with modes `:per_request`, `:watch_file`, `:pool_invalidate`. Default keeps existing perf-oriented behaviour.

zach: sample patch idea:```ruby
# lib/redwood/token_strategy.rb
module Redwood::TokenStrategy
  def auth_header
    case ENV['RB_TOKEN_STRATEGY']
    when 'per_request' then "Bearer #{load_token}"
    else "Bearer #{@cached_token ||= load_token}"
    end
  end
end
```

leo: Also add client API `client.invalidate_auth!` that clears cached token and resets connection pool. That keeps an explicit escape hatch for users who rotate tokens programmatically.

amy: For parity with other SDKs, document that node/go offer a first-class refresh callback hook. Could add a `on_token_rotate` callback option so users can call `invalidate_auth!` automatically.

sdk-bot: lint: rubocop errors in sampleapp demo.rb — run `bundle exec rubocop -a` to fix.

zach: I'll open a PR that: (1) introduces RB_TOKEN_STRATEGY env with `per_request` opt for quickstart, (2) adds `client.invalidate_auth!` method, (3) updates quickstart README and binstub examples to use `chmod 600` on token files and recommend `per_request` for demos.

leo: For tests, add a small integration that forks a child process to simulate binstub semantics and writes new token after fork to ensure client picks it up when using per_request or after calling invalidate_auth!.

amy: One subtlety: per-request token reads hurt throughput for heavy workloads. Make sure docs warn about perf tradeoff and show watch_file approach + SIGHUP handling as a middle ground.

ci-bot: github/actions - ruby-sampleapp CI #4412 triggered by zach - unit/integration/lint queued.

zach: Thanks — will ping when PR is ready. If CI passes we can cherry-pick to the quickstart branch. Appreciate the rapid help :thumbsup:
